rulers-buildings.text: Sita goes to Fatehpur Sikri near Agra. Which Mughal emperor built this city?
rulers-buildings.explanation: Fatehpur Sikri was built by Akbar.

rulers-buildings.text: Assertion (A): Fatehpur Sikri has the Buland Darwaza. Reason (R): Fatehpur Sikri is in Delhi.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
rulers-buildings.explanation: Fatehpur Sikri does have the Buland Darwaza, but it is near Agra and not in Delhi, so R is false.

rulers-buildings.text: Which of these is NOT linked with Akbar?
rulers-buildings.explanation: The Red Fort at Delhi was built by Shah Jahan, not Akbar.

rulers-buildings.text: The Taj Mahal was built by Shah Jahan as a tomb for
rulers-buildings.explanation: Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal in memory of his wife, Mumtaz Mahal.

rulers-buildings.text: On the banks of which river does the Taj Mahal stand?
rulers-buildings.explanation: The Taj Mahal stands on the bank of the Yamuna at Agra.

rulers-buildings.text: Shah Jahan's new city in Delhi, which had the Red Fort and the Jama Masjid, was called
rulers-buildings.explanation: Shahjahanabad was the walled city built by Shah Jahan around the Red Fort and the Jama Masjid.

rulers-buildings.text: In the Red Fort, the Diwan-i-Am was the hall where the emperor
options: met the general public and heard petitions
held a private feast for his family
rulers-buildings.explanation: Diwan-i-Am means Hall of Public Audience, where the ruler met people and listened to their requests.

rulers-buildings.text: Neha compares two buildings of Shah Jahan. One is made mostly of white marble and the other mostly of red sandstone. Which pair is correct, in that order?
rulers-buildings.explanation: The Taj Mahal is white marble and the Red Fort has red sandstone walls. The reverse order is wrong, and the other pairs are not Shah Jahan's.

rulers-buildings.text: Vikram plans a day in Delhi to see two buildings built by Shah Jahan. Which pair should he visit?
rulers-buildings.explanation: The Red Fort and Jama Masjid are both in Delhi and were built by Shah Jahan. The Taj Mahal is in Agra.

rulers-buildings.text: Assertion (A): Shah Jahan built the Jama Masjid in Delhi. Reason (R): Shah Jahan also built the Taj Mahal at Agra.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
rulers-buildings.explanation: Both are true facts, but building the Taj Mahal does not explain why he built the Jama Masjid.

rulers-buildings.text: A charbagh garden is divided into
rulers-buildings.explanation: Charbagh means four gardens: the plan is divided into four parts by walkways or water channels.

rulers-buildings.text: Which of these Mughal-period buildings has a charbagh garden?
rulers-buildings.explanation: The Taj Mahal is set in a charbagh garden. The other three are not garden monuments.

rulers-buildings.text: Which of these is NOT true about a charbagh?
options: It is a tall tower built with lime mortar
It is a garden divided into four parts
Walkways or channels of water separate the parts
Mughal builders used it around tombs
rulers-buildings.explanation: A charbagh is a garden plan, not a tower.

rulers-buildings.text: Hampi, once the capital of the Vijayanagara empire, lies on the banks of the river
rulers-buildings.explanation: Hampi is on the bank of the Tungabhadra in Karnataka.

rulers-buildings.text: The Virupaksha temple at Hampi is dedicated to
rulers-buildings.explanation: Virupaksha is a form of Shiva, and the temple at Hampi is his shrine.

rulers-buildings.text: Deepa visits the ruins at Hampi in Karnataka. Which empire had its capital there?
rulers-buildings.explanation: Hampi was the capital of the Vijayanagara empire.

rulers-buildings.text: Assertion (A): Hampi was the capital of the Vijayanagara empire. Reason (R): The Virupaksha temple at Hampi was built by the Mughals.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
rulers-buildings.explanation: A is true. The Virupaksha temple is a temple of the Vijayanagara period, not a Mughal building, so R is false.

rulers-buildings.text: Which of these is NOT true about Hampi?
options: It was the capital of the Vijayanagara empire
It lies on the banks of the Yamuna
rulers-buildings.explanation: Hampi is on the Tungabhadra, not the Yamuna.

rulers-buildings.text: The temples at Thanjavur and Hampi in the south were built mostly of
rulers-buildings.explanation: Southern temples such as Rajarajeshvara and Virupaksha were raised with stone.

rulers-buildings.text: Assertion (A): Buildings in different regions of India had different styles. Reason (R): Builders used local materials and local craft traditions.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
rulers-buildings.explanation: Local materials and skills shaped what builders made, so buildings in different regions looked different.

rulers-buildings.text: Tarun sees that Delhi's Sultanate monuments use arches and domes, while the Thanjavur temple uses lintels and a tall tower. What does this suggest?
options: Different regions and rulers followed different building styles
All builders used one common plan
Arches were unknown everywhere in India
rulers-buildings.explanation: Buildings of this age show regional styles, since builders used the methods and traditions of their own region.

rulers-buildings.text: Why did rulers build grand temples and mosques, as the chapter explains?
options: To show their devotion and also their power and wealth
rulers-buildings.explanation: Rulers built them for religious reasons and also to show power, wealth and prestige.

rulers-buildings.text: Besides palaces and temples, which of these did kings also build for the public?
rulers-buildings.explanation: Rulers also built tanks, wells and bazaars. Railways and telegraphs came much later.

rulers-buildings.text: A king builds a huge temple in his capital and invites many pilgrims to see it. Neighbouring kings hear of it and admire him. Besides worship, what does this show?
options: Building grand monuments brought the ruler fame and prestige
Temples were built only by traders
Rulers never cared about their reputation
Pilgrims paid for the whole temple
rulers-buildings.explanation: Grand buildings were a way for rulers to win fame, prestige and the respect of others.

rulers-buildings.text: Assertion (A): Rulers built big temples and mosques only to worship; they never wanted to show their power. Reason (R): Grand buildings brought rulers fame and prestige, and showed their wealth.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
rulers-buildings.explanation: A is false because rulers also wanted to show power. R is true, since grand buildings gave fame and prestige.

rulers-buildings.text: Which of these is NOT a reason why rulers built grand monuments?
options: To stop craftspeople from finding work
rulers-buildings.explanation: Grand buildings gave work to many craftspeople. Stopping them was never a reason.

rulers-buildings.text: Who actually carved the stone and raised the walls of great monuments?
options: Only the king and his queens
Only the soldiers of the army
Masons, stone carvers and other craftspeople
Only the merchants of the capital
rulers-buildings.explanation: Rulers ordered and paid for the buildings, but skilled masons, carvers and craftspeople did the work.

rulers-buildings.text: A person who plans a building and guides how it is built is called
rulers-buildings.explanation: An architect designs a building, and masons and craftspeople then build it.

rulers-buildings.text: Rahim says the Qutb Minar was built entirely by the Sultan himself. His teacher disagrees. What is the best correction?
options: The Sultan built it alone with his own hands
The Sultan ordered and paid for it, but masons, carvers and architects built it
Nobody knows who worked on it
rulers-buildings.explanation: Rulers were patrons who gave the orders and the money, while skilled workers did the building.

environment.text: What is meant by the environment?
options: Only the plants and animals around us
Only the buildings of a city
Everything around us, living and non-living, that affects our life
Only the weather of a place
environment.explanation: The environment is our surroundings: land, water, air, plants, animals, buildings and people.

environment.text: Which of these is part of the natural environment?
environment.explanation: A river is made by nature. Railway tracks, parks and bridges are built by people.

environment.text: Which of these is a human-made environment?
environment.explanation: A bridge is built by people, while mountains, rivers and forests are natural.

environment.text: The solid, rocky outer layer of the earth is called the:
environment.explanation: The lithosphere is the solid crust of the earth made of rocks and soil.

environment.text: Oceans, rivers and lakes together form which domain of the earth?
environment.explanation: The hydrosphere is the domain of water on the earth.

environment.text: The thin layer of air around the earth is called the:
environment.explanation: The atmosphere is the envelope of air that surrounds the earth.

environment.text: Which gas in the air do living beings need for breathing?
environment.explanation: Humans and animals breathe in oxygen from the air.

environment.text: Loud horns, loudspeakers and heavy machines cause which type of pollution?
environment.explanation: Unwanted loud sound is called noise pollution.

environment.text: Which of these is a renewable resource?
environment.explanation: Wind is replaced by nature again and again, so it is renewable. Coal, petroleum and natural gas get used up.

environment.text: Which gas makes up the largest part of the air?
environment.explanation: Air is about 78% nitrogen and about 21% oxygen.

environment.text: About what part of the earth's surface is covered with water?
environment.explanation: Water covers about 71% of the earth's surface and land covers the rest.

environment.text: What is the biosphere?
options: The layer of gases around the earth
The narrow zone where land, water and air meet and support life
The solid crust of the earth
All the water on the earth
environment.explanation: The biosphere is the zone of contact of the lithosphere, hydrosphere and atmosphere where life exists.

environment.text: Which of these is an abiotic component of an ecosystem?
environment.explanation: Abiotic means non-living. Soil is non-living while fish, algae and frogs are living.

environment.text: Which of these is a biotic component of a pond ecosystem?
environment.explanation: Biotic means living. Fish are living things, while water, sunlight and air are non-living.

environment.text: Which statement defines an ecosystem best?
options: A group of only animals living together
All the buildings and roads of a region
The weather of a place over many years
Living things and their non-living surroundings interacting with one another
environment.explanation: An ecosystem is made of biotic and abiotic components that depend on each other.

environment.text: Water vapour cooling to form tiny droplets that make clouds is called:
environment.explanation: Cooling of water vapour into droplets is condensation.

environment.text: Rain, snow and hail falling from clouds are together called:
environment.explanation: Water that falls from clouds to the ground in any form is precipitation.

environment.text: Which of these is a non-renewable resource?
environment.explanation: Coal took millions of years to form and cannot be replaced quickly once used.

environment.text: Glaciers and ice caps are part of which domain?
environment.explanation: The hydrosphere includes water in all forms, including ice.

environment.text: Which of these is an example of the human environment?
options: The relationships among people in a community
environment.explanation: The human environment is about people, their relationships, families and communities.

environment.text: Which action helps keep the environment in balance?
environment.explanation: Planting trees and saving water protect natural resources and keep the balance.

environment.text: Which pair is correctly matched?
environment.explanation: Rivers and lakes are water bodies, so they belong to the hydrosphere.

environment.text: The biosphere is formed by the contact of which domains?
environment.explanation: Life exists where land, water and air meet, so all three domains take part.

environment.text: During evaporation, water moves from which domain into which domain?
options: From the atmosphere into the hydrosphere
From the hydrosphere into the atmosphere
From the lithosphere into the biosphere
From the hydrosphere into the lithosphere
environment.explanation: Water from oceans and rivers turns into vapour and rises into the air.

environment.text: Which pair contains only abiotic components of a forest?
environment.explanation: Sunlight and soil are non-living. Deer, grass, trees and birds are living.

environment.text: Why is the atmosphere important for life on the earth?
options: It provides the air we breathe and protects us from harmful rays of the sun
It gives us rocks and minerals
It stores all the fresh water of the earth
It forms the soil in which plants grow
environment.explanation: The atmosphere has oxygen for breathing and shields living things from harmful sun rays.

environment.text: Which situation shows that the parts of an environment depend on one another?
options: If a pond dries up, the fish and water plants in it also die
environment.explanation: Living things depend on their non-living surroundings, so losing water harms the whole pond.

environment.text: Why is the unplanned growth of cities and cutting of forests harmful?
options: It increases the fresh water on the earth
It destroys the homes of living things and upsets the balance of the environment
It helps all wild animals live in cities
environment.explanation: Clearing forests and spreading cities removes habitats and disturbs the balance of nature.

environment.text: Meena looks around her village and sees a pond, hills, a temple, a road and a school building. Which of these belong to the natural environment?
options: The road and the school building
The temple and the school building
environment.explanation: Ponds and hills are made by nature. Temples, roads and buildings are made by people.

environment.text: Arjun's family in Chennai lives in a flat and travels by metro train. The flat and the metro are examples of the:
environment.explanation: Buildings and trains are made by people, so they form the human-made environment.

environment.text: A factory in Kanpur releases thick black smoke from its chimney all day. Which type of pollution does this cause?
environment.explanation: Smoke mixes with the air and makes it dirty, which is air pollution.

environment.text: In Kerala, the whole village celebrates Onam together and neighbours help each other. Which part of the environment does this show?
environment.explanation: Festivals, customs and relationships among people form the human environment.

environment.text: A factory near Varanasi pours its waste into a river. Fish die and villagers fall sick after drinking the water. Which type of pollution is this?
environment.explanation: Waste added to river water is water pollution, and it harms living things.

environment.text: Gurpreet's class makes a model of a pond with fish, frogs, water plants, water, mud and sunlight. Which list has only the biotic components?
environment.explanation: Biotic components are living things: fish, frogs and water plants.

environment.text: Neha hangs a wet cloth in the sun and it becomes dry. Which step of the water cycle is happening?
environment.explanation: Heat turns the water in the cloth into vapour, which is evaporation.

environment.text: Kabir's city cut many trees to build a wide road. The birds that nested in those trees have disappeared. What is the best explanation?
options: Birds prefer to live near roads
environment.explanation: Cutting trees destroys the habitat of birds, so they leave or die.

environment.text: A village in Rajasthan uses solar panels to make electricity. Why is solar energy called renewable?
options: It is found deep under the ground
It is made by burning coal
Sunlight is not used up by using it
environment.explanation: The sun keeps giving light every day, so solar energy is renewable.

environment.text: Priya's neighbourhood burns heaps of garbage in the open every evening, and people cough a lot. What is the most suitable step?
options: Collect the waste and dispose of or recycle it properly
Burn even more garbage at night
Throw the waste into a nearby river
Bury the waste near the well
environment.explanation: Proper disposal and recycling stop smoke and also avoid polluting water and soil.

environment.text: A farmer in Punjab ploughs his field, sows seeds and irrigates the crop. Which statement is correct?
options: Farming has no effect on the environment
Farming is part of the atmosphere
Farming creates a new ecosystem on another planet
Farming is an interaction between humans and the natural environment
environment.explanation: Farmers use land, water and sunlight, which links people with the natural environment.

environment.text: A pond near Pune has fish, water plants, insects, water, mud and sunlight. A chemical factory dumps waste into it and the fish die. Which statement best shows that an ecosystem is interlinked?
options: Only the fish are affected, nothing else changes
Harm to the water also harms the living things and upsets the whole pond
Dirty water makes the mud living
Sunlight stops the effect of the waste
environment.explanation: All parts of an ecosystem depend on each other, so damage to one part affects the rest.

environment.text: Rohan classifies things into domains: mountain (lithosphere), lake (hydrosphere), oxygen (atmosphere) and cloud (lithosphere). Which of his classifications is wrong?
environment.explanation: Clouds are made of water droplets floating in the air, so they belong to the atmosphere, not the lithosphere.

environment.text: A fast growing city replaces parks with buildings. Residents now see more smoke from vehicles and hear loud honking all day. Which two types of pollution are being described?
environment.explanation: Smoke causes air pollution and honking causes noise pollution.

environment.text: Mohan says all parts of the environment are natural. His teacher says a school playground is human-made and the friendship among students belongs to the human environment. Who is right?
options: Mohan, because everything around us is natural
Neither, because the playground is natural
Mohan, because friendship is a natural object
environment.explanation: Playgrounds are built by people, and relationships among people form the human environment.

environment.text: Sunita's village farm uses a lot of chemicals. The chemicals soak into the soil and reach the water of a nearby well. This is an example of soil pollution reaching which domain?
options: The biosphere, from the hydrosphere only
environment.explanation: The chemicals travel from the soil (lithosphere) into the water (hydrosphere).

environment.text: Which of these is NOT one of the four domains of the earth?
environment.explanation: The four domains are lithosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere and biosphere. The stratosphere is only a layer of the atmosphere.

environment.text: Which of these is NOT a human-made environment?
environment.explanation: A forest grows naturally, while the others are built by people.

environment.text: Which of these is NOT a cause of air pollution?
environment.explanation: Planting trees makes the air cleaner. The other three add harmful smoke to the air.

environment.text: Which of these is NOT a way to protect the environment?
options: Cutting trees without planting new ones
environment.explanation: Cutting trees without replacing them harms the environment.

environment.text: Which of these is NOT part of the hydrosphere?
environment.explanation: Mountains are part of the lithosphere. Rivers, oceans and lakes are water bodies.

environment.text: Which of these is NOT a harmful effect of pollution?
environment.explanation: Pollution makes air and water dirty, so cleaner air and water is not an effect of it.

environment.text: Which of these is NOT an example of humans interacting with the environment?
options: Building a dam on a river
Cutting a road through a hill
environment.explanation: A volcanic eruption happens in nature without human action.

environment.text: Assertion (A): The atmosphere is important for life on the earth. Reason (R): It contains oxygen that living beings need for breathing.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
environment.explanation: The atmosphere supplies oxygen, which is why it is vital for life.

environment.text: Assertion (A): A pond is an example of an ecosystem. Reason (R): A pond has living and non-living components that depend on one another.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
environment.explanation: An ecosystem is a set of living and non-living parts that interact, and a pond fits this.

environment.text: Assertion (A): Water covers most of the earth's surface. Reason (R): Water is necessary for all living things.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
environment.explanation: Both statements are true, but the need for water does not explain how much of the earth it covers.

environment.text: Assertion (A): Noise pollution can harm our hearing. Reason (R): Plastic bags take a very long time to break down.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
environment.explanation: Both are true facts, but the second has nothing to do with hearing.

environment.text: Assertion (A): Burning fuel in vehicles causes air pollution. Reason (R): Vehicles release only clean oxygen into the air.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
environment.explanation: Vehicles release smoke and harmful gases, so R is false while A is true.

environment.text: Assertion (A): Sunlight is a renewable source of energy. Reason (R): Sunlight gets used up and finishes once we use it.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
environment.explanation: Sunlight is not used up by our use, so A is true and R is false.

environment.text: Assertion (A): Rocks and minerals are part of the hydrosphere. Reason (R): The lithosphere is the solid crust of the earth made of rocks and minerals.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
environment.explanation: Rocks and minerals belong to the lithosphere, so A is false, while R is true.

environment.text: Assertion (A): Fish are abiotic components of a pond. Reason (R): Abiotic components are the non-living parts of an ecosystem.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
environment.explanation: Fish are living, so they are biotic. A is false, but R correctly defines abiotic.

environment.text: Assertion (A): Cutting forests on a large scale can upset the balance of the environment. Reason (R): Forests give homes to many living things and help keep air and soil healthy.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
environment.explanation: Forests support wildlife, air and soil, so removing them upsets the balance. R explains A.

inside-our-earth.text: Steel is made mainly from which metal?
inside-our-earth.explanation: Iron, taken from iron ore, is the main material of steel.

inside-our-earth.text: Meena visits the Deccan plateau in Maharashtra and sees a black, fine-grained rock formed when lava cooled on the surface. Which rock is it likely to be?
inside-our-earth.explanation: Basalt is a fine-grained extrusive igneous rock formed from lava that cools on the surface.

inside-our-earth.text: The opening in the Earth's crust through which magma reaches the surface in a volcano is called the
inside-our-earth.explanation: Magma rises through the vent and comes out as lava.

inside-our-earth.text: Assertion (A): The central part of the Earth is called nife. Reason (R): The core is made mainly of nickel and iron.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
inside-our-earth.explanation: Nife is named after nickel (Ni) and iron (Fe), which is exactly what the core is made of.

inside-our-earth.text: Rocks that have changed their form because of great heat and pressure are called
inside-our-earth.explanation: Metamorphic means changed in form; heat and pressure change existing rocks into metamorphic rocks.

inside-our-earth.text: Assertion (A): The crust is the thickest layer of the Earth. Reason (R): The crust is the outermost layer of the Earth.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
inside-our-earth.explanation: A is false because the crust is the thinnest layer; R is true.

inside-our-earth.text: Assertion (A): Fossils are not found in igneous rocks. Reason (R): Igneous rocks form from very hot molten material.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
inside-our-earth.explanation: Remains of living things would be destroyed by molten rock, so igneous rocks do not hold fossils.

inside-our-earth.text: Assertion (A): Sedimentary rocks form when lava cools on the Earth's surface. Reason (R): Extrusive igneous rocks form when lava cools on the Earth's surface.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
inside-our-earth.explanation: A is false because cooled lava forms igneous rock, not sedimentary; R is a true statement.

inside-our-earth.text: Quartzite is formed when which rock is changed by heat and pressure?
inside-our-earth.explanation: Sandstone changes into the hard metamorphic rock quartzite.

inside-our-earth.text: Assertion (A): Temperature rises as we go deeper into the Earth. Reason (R): The inner core is the coolest layer of the Earth.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
inside-our-earth.explanation: A is true; R is false because the inner core is the hottest part.

inside-our-earth.text: Slate is formed when which rock changes?
inside-our-earth.explanation: Clay changes into slate under heat and pressure.

inside-our-earth.text: Which of these best describes a mineral?
options: A man-made material used in factories
A natural substance with a definite chemical composition
inside-our-earth.explanation: Minerals occur naturally and each has a definite chemical composition.

inside-our-earth.text: Assertion (A): Sandstone is a sedimentary rock. Reason (R): Slate is formed from clay.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
inside-our-earth.explanation: Both statements are true, but the formation of slate has nothing to do with sandstone being sedimentary.

inside-our-earth.text: The oceanic crust is also called sima because it is rich in
inside-our-earth.explanation: Sima comes from SIlica and MAgnesium, the main materials of the oceanic crust.

inside-our-earth.text: Near Prakash's island village a volcano has not erupted for hundreds of years, but scientists warn that it may erupt again someday. Such a volcano is called
inside-our-earth.explanation: A dormant volcano is one that is quiet now but may erupt again in the future.

inside-our-earth.text: The Richter scale is used to measure
inside-our-earth.explanation: The Richter scale gives a number for how strong an earthquake is.

inside-our-earth.text: Assertion (A): Granite is an intrusive igneous rock. Reason (R): Basalt is an extrusive igneous rock.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
inside-our-earth.explanation: Both are correct facts, but basalt being extrusive says nothing about why granite is intrusive.

inside-our-earth.text: The bowl-shaped opening at the top of a volcano from which lava erupts is called a
inside-our-earth.explanation: The crater is the opening at the top of the volcano where lava and gases come out.

inside-our-earth.text: Extrusive igneous rocks are formed when
options: magma cools slowly deep inside the crust
lava cools and hardens on the Earth's surface
rocks are changed by heat and pressure
inside-our-earth.explanation: Extrusive means coming out: lava that cools quickly on the surface forms extrusive rocks such as basalt.

inside-our-earth.text: Which of these is NOT related to earthquakes?
inside-our-earth.explanation: A crater belongs to a volcano; focus, epicentre and seismograph are earthquake terms.

inside-our-earth.text: In the rock cycle, rocks that melt deep inside the Earth and then cool and harden become
inside-our-earth.explanation: Melted rock is magma, and when magma cools and solidifies it forms igneous rock.

inside-our-earth.text: Which of these layers of the Earth is in a liquid state?
inside-our-earth.explanation: The outer core is liquid, while the inner core is solid because of the very high pressure.

inside-our-earth.text: Pooja imagines digging straight down from her village on land. Which line correctly names the layer she would be in at depths of 20 km, 1500 km and 3000 km?
inside-our-earth.explanation: The crust is about 35 km thick on land, the mantle goes down to about 2900 km, and the core lies below that.

inside-our-earth.text: The epicentre of an earthquake is
options: the point on the surface directly above the focus
the place inside the crust where the movement starts
the machine that records the waves
the scale on which the strength is measured
inside-our-earth.explanation: The focus is underground; the epicentre is the point on the surface nearest to it, where the shaking is first felt.

inside-our-earth.text: Which mineral is commonly used for making electric wires?
inside-our-earth.explanation: Copper conducts electricity well, so it is used in wires.

inside-our-earth.text: A newspaper says an earthquake began 10 km below the ground near a town in Gujarat. The place below the ground where the earthquake began is called the
inside-our-earth.explanation: The focus is the point underground where the movement starts; the epicentre is the point on the surface above it.

inside-our-earth.text: Neha is told that minerals have many uses. Which pairing of a mineral and its use is correct?
options: Copper, used as a fuel for cooking
inside-our-earth.explanation: Coal is burnt as a fuel; copper is used for wires, iron for steel, and marble is a rock used in buildings.

inside-our-earth.text: What is the hot molten rock found inside the Earth called?
inside-our-earth.explanation: Hot molten rock below the surface is called magma; once it comes out it is called lava.

inside-our-earth.text: Which of these is NOT true about the Earth's core?
options: It is made mainly of nickel and iron
It has very high temperature and pressure
It is rich in silica and alumina, like the continental crust
It lies at the centre of the Earth
inside-our-earth.explanation: Silica and alumina (sial) make up the continental crust; the core is mostly nickel and iron.

inside-our-earth.text: A block of limestone in a quarry is buried deep and changed by heat and pressure. Later it melts and is thrown out by a volcano as lava, which cools. Which sequence of rock types describes this?
inside-our-earth.explanation: Limestone is sedimentary; heat and pressure make it marble (metamorphic); melting and cooling as lava then make it igneous.

inside-our-earth.text: Which layer of the Earth lies just beneath the crust?
inside-our-earth.explanation: The mantle lies between the crust above and the core below.

inside-our-earth.text: Which of these is an igneous rock?
inside-our-earth.explanation: Granite forms when magma cools and hardens, so it is an igneous rock.

inside-our-earth.text: In which type of rock are fossils usually found?
inside-our-earth.explanation: Remains of plants and animals get buried in layers of sediment, which harden into sedimentary rock.

inside-our-earth.text: Which is the outermost layer of the Earth?
inside-our-earth.explanation: The crust is the thin, solid outer skin of the Earth on which we live.

inside-our-earth.text: Which part of the Earth is called sial?
inside-our-earth.explanation: The continental crust is rich in silica and alumina, so it is called sial.

inside-our-earth.text: At an observatory in Pune, Sanjay sees a machine that draws zigzag lines whenever the ground shakes. What is this machine called?
inside-our-earth.explanation: A seismograph records the vibrations (seismic waves) of an earthquake.

inside-our-earth.text: Why are igneous rocks called primary rocks?
options: They are always found at the top of hills
They are formed only from sediments
They are the first rocks to form, and other rocks are formed from them
inside-our-earth.explanation: Igneous rocks form first from cooling magma; sedimentary and metamorphic rocks are formed later from other rocks.

inside-our-earth.text: Which part of the Earth is the hottest?
inside-our-earth.explanation: Temperature rises with depth, so the centre (the core) is the hottest part.

inside-our-earth.text: Pebbles from a granite hill in Himachal are washed down by a stream and settle on a riverbed in layers. Over a very long time they are pressed and cemented into rock. What type of rock forms?
inside-our-earth.explanation: Fragments of old rock that are carried by water, deposited in layers and compacted form sedimentary rock.

inside-our-earth.text: Marble is formed from which rock?
inside-our-earth.explanation: Heat and pressure change limestone into marble.

inside-our-earth.text: The core of the Earth is called nife because it is made mainly of
inside-our-earth.explanation: Nife comes from NIckel and FE (iron), the two main materials of the core.

inside-our-earth.text: The Earth's crust is broken into several large pieces that move very slowly. These pieces are called
inside-our-earth.explanation: The moving slabs of the crust are called plates.

inside-our-earth.text: Which of these is NOT a layer of the Earth's interior?
inside-our-earth.explanation: The atmosphere is the air around the Earth, not a layer inside it.

inside-our-earth.text: Vibrations that travel outwards from the focus of an earthquake are called
inside-our-earth.explanation: The shaking that spreads from the focus through the Earth is carried by seismic waves.

inside-our-earth.text: Which of these is NOT true about the Earth's crust?
options: The continental crust is called sima
It is thinner under the oceans than under the continents
It is the thinnest layer of the Earth
inside-our-earth.explanation: The continental crust is called sial; the oceanic crust is sima.

inside-our-earth.text: A scientist wants to drill through the crust to reach the mantle. She can choose a spot on a continent or on the ocean floor. Which is the better choice and why?
options: Continent, because the crust there is thinner
Ocean floor, because the crust there is about 35 km thick
Ocean floor, because the crust is only about 5 km thick there
Either place, because the crust is equally thick everywhere
inside-our-earth.explanation: The oceanic crust is about 5 km thick, much thinner than the continental crust of about 35 km.

inside-our-earth.text: Hari's father is a mason in Nashik who builds houses with stone. Hari's teacher says that every rock is made up of one or more of what?
inside-our-earth.explanation: Rocks are made up of one or more minerals.

inside-our-earth.text: A guide at the Taj Mahal in Agra tells visitors that the white marble was once limestone. What changed limestone into marble?
options: Great heat and pressure inside the Earth
Layers of sand settling in a river
Wind carrying sediments over many years
inside-our-earth.explanation: Heat and pressure change limestone, a sedimentary rock, into marble, a metamorphic rock.

inside-our-earth.text: Assertion (A): Earthquakes can be caused by the movement of plates. Reason (R): The Earth's crust is broken into plates that keep moving slowly.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
inside-our-earth.explanation: Because the crust is made of slowly moving plates, their movement can shake the surface and cause earthquakes.

inside-our-earth.text: The crust under the continents is about how thick?
inside-our-earth.explanation: The crust is about 35 km thick on the continents and only about 5 km thick under the oceans.

inside-our-earth.text: The mantle extends up to a depth of about
inside-our-earth.explanation: Below the crust the mantle goes down to about 2900 km, where the core begins.

inside-our-earth.text: Riya reads that the Earth's crust is broken into huge slabs called plates that keep moving slowly. Which of these can happen when plates move?
options: The Moon moves closer to the Earth
Sandstone turns into magma at once
inside-our-earth.explanation: The movement of plates can shake the Earth's surface and cause earthquakes.

inside-our-earth.text: Workers in a very deep gold mine in South Africa say that the rock at the bottom is much hotter than at the top. What does this show?
options: Temperature falls as we go deeper into the Earth
Temperature rises as we go deeper into the Earth
Temperature is the same at every depth
inside-our-earth.explanation: The deeper we go below the surface, the hotter it gets.

inside-our-earth.text: Which pair (original rock, rock it changes into) is NOT correct?
inside-our-earth.explanation: Slate comes from clay; limestone changes into marble.

inside-our-earth.text: Fatima's grandmother has an old grinding stone made of granite. Fatima sees that it has large crystals. What explains the large crystals?
options: Lava cooled very fast after an eruption
Layers of sand were pressed together
Clay was changed by heat and pressure
The magma cooled slowly deep inside the crust
inside-our-earth.explanation: Granite is an intrusive igneous rock: slow cooling inside the Earth gives time for large crystals to grow.

inside-our-earth.text: Assertion (A): Lava is magma that has reached the Earth's surface. Reason (R): Lava is found only deep inside the Earth, far below the crust.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
inside-our-earth.explanation: A is true; R is false because lava is the molten rock that has come out onto the surface.

inside-our-earth.text: Which of these is NOT a metamorphic rock?
inside-our-earth.explanation: Limestone is a sedimentary rock; marble, slate and quartzite are metamorphic.

inside-our-earth.text: Anita finds a rock with clear layers of sand grains and the imprint of a fish. Her friend says it is igneous. Which reason best shows the friend is wrong?
options: Igneous rocks are always black in colour
Igneous rocks only form under the sea
Igneous rocks form from hot molten material, so they would not hold sediment layers or the imprint of a living thing
Igneous rocks are never found on land
inside-our-earth.explanation: Layers and fossils belong to sedimentary rocks; the heat of molten rock would destroy such remains.

inside-our-earth.text: Which of these is NOT true of sedimentary rocks?
options: They are formed directly by the cooling of magma
They are formed from sediments pressed together
inside-our-earth.explanation: Cooling of magma makes igneous rocks; sedimentary rocks are made from compacted sediments.

inside-our-earth.text: Ramesh finds a rock on a river bank near Patna. It is made of thin layers and crumbles into sand grains when rubbed. Which type of rock is it most likely to be?
inside-our-earth.explanation: Layers of sand deposited by water and pressed together form sedimentary rock such as sandstone.

on-equality.text: Which principle is the basis of universal adult franchise?
options: Men and women vote on different days
on-equality.explanation: Universal adult franchise means every adult gets exactly one vote, whoever they are.

on-equality.text: What is the minimum age at which an Indian citizen can vote in elections?
on-equality.explanation: In India all citizens who are 18 years or older have the right to vote.

on-equality.text: How does the vote of a rich landowner compare with the vote of a poor labourer in an Indian election?
options: The landowner's vote has more value
The labourer's vote has more value
The value depends on how much education the voter has
on-equality.explanation: Every vote counts equally. Wealth, caste or education does not change the value of a vote.

on-equality.text: Which Article of the Constitution says that all persons are equal before the law?
on-equality.explanation: Article 14 guarantees equality before the law to every person.

on-equality.text: Which Article of the Constitution abolishes untouchability?
on-equality.explanation: Article 17 declares that untouchability is abolished and its practice in any form is forbidden.

on-equality.text: Article 15 of the Constitution says that the government cannot:
options: Discriminate against a person on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth
Hold elections more than once in five years
on-equality.explanation: Article 15 forbids discrimination on the grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth.

on-equality.text: The right to equality in India is part of the:
on-equality.explanation: Equality before the law and freedom from discrimination are Fundamental Rights, guaranteed by the Constitution.

on-equality.text: What does the word "dignity" mean?
options: Being respected and valued as a person
on-equality.explanation: Dignity is the feeling of being respected and of being worth something, and every person deserves it.

on-equality.text: Many domestic workers are poor and their work is looked down upon. How are they often treated?
options: They are treated as inferior and not given proper respect
They are treated with more respect than their employers
They are always given a seat at the dining table
They are paid more than all other workers
on-equality.explanation: Domestic workers often face unequal treatment and a lack of respect, which is an example of inequality in everyday life.

on-equality.text: People who were treated as "untouchable" because of their caste, and who faced discrimination for centuries, are today commonly called:
on-equality.explanation: Dalits is the name commonly used for the groups that suffered untouchability and caste discrimination.

on-equality.text: What does the mid-day meal scheme give to children in government schools?
options: A free cooked meal at school
on-equality.explanation: Under the mid-day meal scheme, children in government primary schools get a cooked meal at school.

on-equality.text: How does the mid-day meal scheme help to bring equality?
options: It gives rich children more marks
It stops children from going to school
It lets only some castes eat together
Poor children get a meal and can attend school and learn without being hungry
on-equality.explanation: A free meal helps poor children come to school regularly and study, and children sit and eat together.

on-equality.text: What is the main aim of the Persons with Disabilities Act?
options: To give people with disabilities equal rights and opportunities
To keep them away from public places
on-equality.explanation: The Act was passed to make sure that people with disabilities enjoy equal rights and can take part fully in society.

on-equality.text: Which of these helps a wheelchair user to enter a public building?
on-equality.explanation: A ramp lets wheelchair users move in and out of buildings, so it supports equal access.

on-equality.text: Which idea lies at the heart of equality in a democracy?
options: Everyone must do the same work
Everyone must earn the same money
Every person is of equal worth and deserves equal respect
Everyone must follow the same religion
on-equality.explanation: In a democracy all persons are equal citizens with equal rights and dignity, whatever their background.

on-equality.text: Universal adult franchise gives the right to vote to:
options: Only those who pay income tax
Only those who can read and write
on-equality.explanation: Universal adult franchise means that all adult citizens can vote, with no conditions of wealth, education, caste or religion.

on-equality.text: Which of these must be open to every person without discrimination, as the Constitution says?
options: Shops, restaurants, roads and public wells
The private home of a neighbour
A club meant for its own members
Only the temples of one's own religion
on-equality.explanation: The Constitution says every person can use public places such as shops, restaurants, wells and roads, whatever their caste, religion or sex.

on-equality.text: How does the government work to promote equality?
options: By making laws and running schemes
By giving everyone the same salary
By asking people to change their religion
on-equality.explanation: The government passes laws and runs programmes, such as the mid-day meal scheme, to help people who are treated unequally.

on-equality.text: The Constitution promises equality, yet many people still face discrimination. What does this show?
options: Equality is not needed in a democracy
Laws have no value at all
Laws must be followed in practice and people's attitudes must also change
on-equality.explanation: Laws give a strong base, but real equality needs people to follow them and give up prejudice in daily life.

on-equality.text: Which of these is an example of inequality caused by poverty?
options: Two friends like different school subjects
One child likes cricket and another likes football
Two cousins live in different cities
A poor child leaves school to earn money while a richer child continues studying
on-equality.explanation: Poverty can take away chances such as education, which makes some children unequal to others.

on-equality.text: Dalit movements have mainly demanded:
options: Dignity, equal rights and an end to untouchability
on-equality.explanation: Dalit movements have struggled for respect, equal treatment and an end to caste discrimination.

on-equality.text: The disability rights movement has demanded:
options: Separate buildings that others cannot use
Equal access to education, jobs and public places
No part in decisions about their lives
Lower wages for the same work
on-equality.explanation: People with disabilities have asked for equal rights, including ramps, schools and jobs open to them.

on-equality.text: Articles 14 to 18 of the Constitution together give the:
on-equality.explanation: Equality before the law (Article 14), no discrimination (Article 15) and the abolition of untouchability (Article 17) are part of the Right to Equality.

on-equality.text: Why did India choose universal adult franchise?
options: So that only the rich can choose rulers
So that elections can be avoided
So that only educated people take part
So that every adult has a say in choosing the government
on-equality.explanation: In a democracy every adult citizen is equal, so every adult is given a vote.

on-equality.text: Who was the chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Indian Constitution?
on-equality.explanation: Dr B. R. Ambedkar headed the Drafting Committee, and the Constitution gives every person equal rights.

on-equality.text: On which date did the Constitution of India come into force?
on-equality.explanation: The Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950, which we celebrate as Republic Day.

on-equality.text: Which of these best describes discrimination?
options: Treating everyone with the same rules
Treating people unfairly because of their caste, religion, sex or other identity
on-equality.explanation: Discrimination means unfair treatment of a person because of the group they belong to.

on-equality.text: What does "equality before the law" mean?
options: The law applies only to the poor
Rich people get a lighter punishment
Judges can favour people of their own caste
The same law applies to every person, whether rich or poor
on-equality.explanation: Equality before the law means no one is above the law and no one is treated differently by it.

on-equality.text: Priya turned 18 last month and has studied only up to Class 5. Her neighbour says she cannot vote because she is not well educated. What is true?
options: Priya cannot vote until she finishes Class 10
Priya can vote, because education is not a condition for voting
Priya can vote only if her family owns land
Priya can vote only after she turns 21
on-equality.explanation: Universal adult franchise gives every adult citizen of 18 or more the right to vote, whatever their education.

on-equality.text: Sunita works as a domestic worker in Mrs Verma's house in Delhi. She is given her tea in a separate cup kept outside and is never allowed to sit down. What is being denied to her?
on-equality.explanation: Being treated as inferior and denied basic respect is a lack of dignity.

on-equality.text: A restaurant owner in Pune refuses to serve a customer because of his caste. Which Article of the Constitution does this go against?
on-equality.explanation: Article 15 says that no one can be stopped from using shops and public restaurants because of caste, religion, race, sex or place of birth.

on-equality.text: In a village, the families of a Dalit community are not allowed to draw water from the common well. Which practice is this, and what does the Constitution say about it?
options: A local custom, which is protected by Article 17
Untouchability, which is abolished by Article 17
A tax, which is allowed by Article 14
A school rule, which is made by Article 15
on-equality.explanation: Refusing a group access to a public well is a form of untouchability, which Article 17 abolishes.

on-equality.text: In Asha's house, her brother is sent to school but she is told that girls need not study. On which ground is Asha being discriminated against?
on-equality.explanation: Treating a girl unequally only because she is a girl is discrimination on the ground of sex, which Article 15 forbids.

on-equality.text: A government school in Tamil Nadu begins to serve a hot cooked lunch to every child. Attendance of poor children goes up. What is this an example of?
options: A law that removes the right to vote
A step that stops children from studying
A rule that helps only rich children
A government scheme that helps poor children and promotes equality
on-equality.explanation: The mid-day meal scheme is a programme through which the government helps poor children to attend school.

on-equality.text: Imran uses a wheelchair. The town library has only steps at the entrance, so he cannot go in. Which change would best follow the spirit of the Persons with Disabilities Act?
options: Building a ramp at the entrance
Asking Imran to stay at home
on-equality.explanation: The Act aims at equal access to public places, and a ramp lets wheelchair users enter like everyone else.

on-equality.text: A police officer in Lucknow lets a rich man go after he breaks a traffic rule, but fines a poor vendor for the same mistake. Which principle has been broken?
on-equality.explanation: Under Article 14 the same law applies to rich and poor alike, so treating them differently breaks equality before the law.

on-equality.text: Rohan studies in a school with computers, a library and a playground. Salma studies in a school with a leaking roof and no benches. Both live in the same city. What does this show?
options: Inequality in everyday life, where children have unequal chances
on-equality.explanation: The difference in school facilities shows how unequal opportunities can be, which is a form of inequality in daily life.

on-equality.text: On election day in a village in Bihar, a landlord, Mr Singh, says his vote should count for more because he owns 50 acres of land. His labourer Raju also votes. What is correct?
options: Mr Singh's vote counts for more
Each has one vote and both votes have equal value
Raju cannot vote because he owns no land
on-equality.explanation: In India each adult has one vote and every vote has equal value, whatever the voter owns.

on-equality.text: Villagers from a Dalit community in a district join together peacefully, hold meetings and demand entry to a public water tank. What does this show?
options: Equality is given only by the rich
Laws do not matter at all
People can struggle together to demand and win equal rights
Protests are not allowed in a democracy
on-equality.explanation: Many movements for equality have been led by ordinary people who joined hands to demand dignity and rights.

on-equality.text: Mohan says, "If India is a country of equals, everyone must earn exactly the same money." What is the best answer?
options: He is right, and the Constitution says so
Equality means only that all people must live in the same place
Equality means only that every adult must vote twice
Equality means equal rights and equal dignity, not equal income
on-equality.explanation: Equality in a democracy means that every person has equal rights and is treated with respect, which is different from having the same wealth.

on-equality.text: Rahim is 17 years old and wants to vote in the next election. When will he first get the right to vote?
on-equality.explanation: The voting age is 18, so Rahim can vote once he turns 18.

on-equality.text: A group of people with disabilities in a town join together and campaign for ramps, accessible buses and equal chances of jobs. This is an example of:
options: The disability rights movement, a struggle for equality
An election for a village head
A way to avoid paying taxes
on-equality.explanation: Campaigns by people with disabilities for equal access and opportunities are part of the disability rights movement.

on-equality.text: In class, some children laugh at Gopal and call him names because he walks with crutches. What is wrong with this?
options: Nothing is wrong, it is only a joke
It is a way to promote equality
It hurts his dignity, as every person deserves respect
It helps him to vote better
on-equality.explanation: Making fun of a person because of a disability takes away their dignity and treats them unequally.

on-equality.text: In a class election, the teacher gives three votes each to a few students who are class monitors and one vote to the rest. Which basic democratic principle does this go against?
on-equality.explanation: Universal adult franchise rests on one person, one vote, so giving some people extra votes breaks equality.

on-equality.text: Assertion (A): In India every adult citizen can vote, whatever their caste, religion or wealth. Reason (R): India follows the principle of universal adult franchise.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
on-equality.explanation: Universal adult franchise means all adults can vote, which is exactly why caste, religion or wealth does not matter.

on-equality.text: Assertion (A): Untouchability is a punishable offence in India. Reason (R): Article 17 of the Constitution abolishes untouchability.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
on-equality.explanation: Because Article 17 abolishes untouchability, practising it is against the law and punishable.

on-equality.text: Assertion (A): Article 14 says that all persons are equal before the law. Reason (R): The Constitution of India came into force on 26 January 1950.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
on-equality.explanation: Both statements are true, but the date has nothing to do with explaining what Article 14 says.

on-equality.text: Assertion (A): A person of 18 years who owns no property can vote in India. Reason (R): Only people who own property are allowed to vote in India.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
on-equality.explanation: The voting age is 18 and property is not a condition, so A is true and R is false.

on-equality.text: Assertion (A): Article 15 allows shops to refuse customers on the ground of caste. Reason (R): Article 15 prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
on-equality.explanation: A is false because Article 15 forbids such a refusal, and R correctly states what the Article says.

on-equality.text: Assertion (A): A domestic worker deserves the same respect as her employer. Reason (R): In a democracy every person has equal dignity.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
on-equality.explanation: Because every person has equal dignity, a domestic worker is entitled to the same respect as anyone else.

on-equality.text: Assertion (A): Equality in a democracy means that all people must earn the same salary. Reason (R): Equality means that every person has equal rights and is treated with equal dignity.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
on-equality.explanation: A is false because equality is about rights and respect, not equal incomes, while R is a correct statement.

on-equality.text: Assertion (A): The mid-day meal scheme is an example of the government working to promote equality. Reason (R): It gives poor children a meal at school, so that hunger does not keep them away from learning.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
on-equality.explanation: By removing hunger as a hurdle, the scheme gives poor children a fairer chance to study, which promotes equality.

on-equality.text: Assertion (A): The Persons with Disabilities Act aims to give people with disabilities equal rights. Reason (R): Under this Act, people with disabilities are kept away from public life.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
on-equality.explanation: A is true because the Act is meant to ensure equal rights, but R is false since the Act wants them to take part fully.

on-equality.text: Which of these is NOT a ground on which Article 15 forbids discrimination?
on-equality.explanation: Article 15 lists religion, race, caste, sex and place of birth, and favourite food is not a ground of discrimination in it.

on-equality.text: Which of these is NOT an example of treating a domestic worker with dignity?
options: Giving her food in a separate plate kept outside
Letting her sit down and rest
on-equality.explanation: Giving food in a separate plate keeps her apart and shows disrespect, so it is not treating her with dignity.

on-equality.text: Which of these is NOT a feature of universal adult franchise?
on-equality.explanation: Under universal adult franchise no one gets extra votes for being rich, so this cannot be a feature.

on-equality.text: Which of these is NOT a step taken by the government to promote equality?
options: Allowing only some castes to use public wells
Passing the Persons with Disabilities Act
on-equality.explanation: Allowing only some castes to use public wells is discrimination and is against the Constitution.

on-equality.text: Which of these is NOT a public place that Article 15 says everyone can freely use?
options: The private home of a neighbour
on-equality.explanation: Article 15 covers public places such as shops, restaurants, roads and wells, but not private homes.

on-equality.text: Which of these is NOT an example of discrimination?
options: A person is refused entry into a shop because of religion
A girl is stopped from going to school only because she is a girl
A police officer fines every driver who breaks a traffic rule, rich or poor
A person is stopped from drawing water from a public well because of caste
on-equality.explanation: Applying the same rule to everyone is equality before the law, while the other three treat people unfairly because of who they are.

on-equality.text: Which of these is NOT a demand of the disability rights movement?
options: Separate buildings that others cannot enter
on-equality.explanation: The movement asks for equal access and inclusion, not for separate places that keep people apart.

markets-around-us.text: A packet of biscuits has MRP Rs 20 printed on it. What does MRP mean?
options: Minimum Retail Price, the lowest price at which it may be sold
Maximum Retail Price, the highest price at which the packet may be sold
Market Rate Per kilo, the price of one kilo of biscuits
Maker's Reward Price, a prize given to the factory
markets-around-us.explanation: MRP is the Maximum Retail Price, so a shopkeeper cannot charge more than this.

markets-around-us.text: What is a weekly market?
options: A market that is open every day of the week in the same shop
A market that is held only once a year during a fair
A market that is held on one particular day of the week
A big building with many shops on different floors
markets-around-us.explanation: A weekly market is set up on a fixed day each week, and the traders there have no permanent shops.

markets-around-us.text: How is a shopping complex different from a weekly market?
options: It is held only on one particular day
Its traders have no fixed shop
It sells goods only to wholesale traders
Its shops are permanent and open on most days, not on one day of the week
markets-around-us.explanation: A shopping complex has permanent shops that stay open on most days, unlike a weekly market that appears only on one day.

markets-around-us.text: Kabir notices that a wholesale trader sells rice at Rs 44 a kg, but the neighbourhood shopkeeper sells it at Rs 50 a kg. Which is the best reason for the shopkeeper's higher price?
options: The shopkeeper has expenses and needs to earn something for selling in small quantities
The shopkeeper is forbidden from selling at a lower price
Rice is cheaper only on market days
The wholesale trader buys the rice from consumers
markets-around-us.explanation: The shopkeeper buys from the wholesaler and must cover his own costs and earn a little, so his price is higher.

markets-around-us.text: What happens when you buy a notebook from a shop?
options: The buyer gives goods and the seller gives money
The buyer pays money and the seller gives the goods
The seller gives the goods and receives nothing
Both the buyer and the seller give money to each other
markets-around-us.explanation: A market works on exchange: money passes from the buyer to the seller, and goods pass from the seller to the buyer.

markets-around-us.text: What does bargaining mean?
options: The seller fixes a price and the buyer must pay it
The buyer takes the goods without paying
The buyer and the seller discuss the price until they agree on one
The government decides the price of the goods
markets-around-us.explanation: In bargaining, the buyer and seller talk about the price and settle on an amount both accept.

markets-around-us.text: Why do traders in weekly markets not have a fixed shop?
options: The law forbids traders from owning a shop
They can sell goods only once in a lifetime
They sell only services and never goods
They set up temporary stalls on market days and move to other places on other days
markets-around-us.explanation: These traders carry their goods from market to market, putting up a stall on each market day.

markets-around-us.text: Assertion (A): Bargaining is common in weekly markets. Reason (R): Goods in a mall are sold at fixed prices.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
markets-around-us.explanation: Both are true, but fixed mall prices do not explain why bargaining happens in weekly markets.

markets-around-us.text: Who is a hawker?
options: A seller who goes from place to place carrying goods and has no fixed shop
A trader who buys goods in large quantities and sells to shopkeepers
A shopkeeper who owns a shop in a mall
A person who buys goods only for his own use
markets-around-us.explanation: A hawker moves through streets with goods on a cart, cycle or head, and does not have a permanent shop.

markets-around-us.text: Which statement tells goods and services apart correctly?
options: Goods are free of cost, while services must always be paid for
Goods are things we can touch and own, while a service is work done for us
A service is a thing we carry home, while goods are work done for us
Goods are sold only in malls and services only in weekly markets
markets-around-us.explanation: Goods are physical things like rice or shoes, while services are jobs done for us, like stitching or teaching.

markets-around-us.text: Which of these is NOT true of hawkers?
options: They move around with goods on carts, cycles or their heads
They buy goods in huge lots and sell only to retail shops
They often sell goods at people's doors
markets-around-us.explanation: Hawkers sell directly to people, not in huge lots to retail shops; that is what wholesalers do.

markets-around-us.text: What is one advantage of a neighbourhood shop over a weekly market?
options: It always sells goods at lower prices than the weekly market
It moves to a new place each day so more people can reach it
It sells goods only in large quantities
It is near our home and open on most days, so we can buy things when we need them
markets-around-us.explanation: Neighbourhood shops are close by and open most days, which makes them handy for daily needs.

markets-around-us.text: Why are prices in a weekly market usually lower than in a permanent shop?
options: Traders do not have to pay for a permanent shop, so their expenses are less
The government fixes a lower price for every weekly market
Traders get all their goods free from farmers
Buyers in weekly markets do not have to pay money
markets-around-us.explanation: Weekly market traders save on rent and other costs of a permanent shop, so they can sell at lower prices.

markets-around-us.text: People who grow or make the goods that are sold in the market are called
markets-around-us.explanation: Producers are the ones who grow or make goods, such as farmers and weavers.

markets-around-us.text: Farida is studying at home when a man pushing a cart calls out, 'Toys! Balloons!' in her street. He has no shop. What is he called?
markets-around-us.explanation: A seller who moves around with goods and has no fixed shop is a hawker.

markets-around-us.text: Cotton grown in a village is finally sold as a shirt in a city shop. What does this show about markets?
options: Markets work only inside the same village
Markets make every producer earn the same amount
Markets are needed only for goods that cannot be carried
Markets link people in distant places through a chain of buying and selling
markets-around-us.explanation: Many people in different places, from farmers to shopkeepers, are connected by buying and selling the product.

markets-around-us.text: Gopal grows cotton in his village. The cotton passes through a trader, a mill, a cloth maker and a garment shop before becoming a shirt sold for Rs 600 in a city mall. Gopal received only a small part of Rs 600. What does this show?
options: Many people in the chain earn from the shirt, and the producer often gets a small share of the final price
All the people in the chain, including Gopal, earn equal shares of Rs 600
The mall owner grew the cotton
The price of the shirt did not depend on anyone in the chain
markets-around-us.explanation: Each person in the chain earns something, and a small producer like Gopal often ends up with only a small share.

markets-around-us.text: What is a market?
options: A place where only farmers sell crops to each other
A place or arrangement where buyers and sellers meet to exchange goods and services
A building that has only expensive shops
A government office that fixes the price of all goods
markets-around-us.explanation: A market is any place or arrangement that brings buyers and sellers together to exchange goods and services.

markets-around-us.text: When does a trader earn a profit?
options: When he sells goods for less than the money spent on them
When he buys goods but does not sell any
When he sells goods for more than the cost of buying them and his expenses
When he keeps his shop open for more hours than other shops
markets-around-us.explanation: A profit is what remains after the selling price covers the cost of the goods and the trader's expenses.

markets-around-us.text: Assertion (A): A weekly market is held on a particular day of the week. Reason (R): Traders in a weekly market have a permanent shop in the market.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
markets-around-us.explanation: A is true because weekly markets meet on a fixed day, but R is false because the traders there have no permanent shop.

markets-around-us.text: Which of these is NOT a service?
markets-around-us.explanation: A packet of biscuits is a good, while the others are work done for us.

markets-around-us.text: Assertion (A): A retail trader sells goods to consumers. Reason (R): A retail trader buys goods only from consumers.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
markets-around-us.explanation: A is true, but R is false because a retail trader buys from wholesalers or producers, not from consumers.

markets-around-us.text: Sheela buys a packet with MRP Rs 20 printed on it, but the shopkeeper asks for Rs 25. What should she do?
options: Point out that the price cannot be more than the MRP and ask for the printed price
Pay Rs 25 because the shopkeeper decides the price
Offer Rs 10 because all buyers must bargain
markets-around-us.explanation: The MRP is the highest price allowed, so a seller cannot ask for more than it.

markets-around-us.text: A shirt costs Rs 600 in a shop. Which of these is part of what the buyer is paying for?
options: Only the money that the cotton farmer asked for
The cost of making, carrying and selling the shirt, along with the traders' earnings
Only the cost of the cloth
markets-around-us.explanation: The price covers every step in the chain, including making, transport, selling costs and what the traders earn.

markets-around-us.text: Shyam grows tomatoes and sells them to Pramod, who sells them to Geeta, the shopkeeper. Mrs Nair buys the tomatoes from Geeta to cook at home. Who is the consumer in this chain?
markets-around-us.explanation: The consumer is the person who buys the goods to use them, and that is Mrs Nair.

markets-around-us.text: A trader sells packs marked 'one kilo' of sugar that really weigh only 900 g. Why do we need rules and checks on markets?
options: Rules make every shop sell at the same price
Rules stop poor people from becoming sellers
Rules are needed only in malls, not in weekly markets
Without rules, ordinary buyers could be cheated through false weights, quality or prices
markets-around-us.explanation: Rules and checks protect ordinary buyers from unfair practices like false weights.

markets-around-us.text: Which place usually sells goods at fixed prices, with shops on several floors of one building?
markets-around-us.explanation: A mall is a large, often air-conditioned building with many shops on different floors and fixed prices.

markets-around-us.text: Which of these is NOT a sign of a fair market?
options: Sellers charge no more than the MRP printed on the pack
Small producers are forced to take very low prices because they have no other choice
Sellers give the correct weight of goods
Buyers can compare prices and choose where to buy
markets-around-us.explanation: A fair market does not leave small producers with no choice but to accept very low prices.

markets-around-us.text: Which statement is true of a retail trader?
options: He sells only huge lots to other traders
He grows the goods that he sells
He sells goods in small quantities to consumers
He never has a shop or a stall
markets-around-us.explanation: A retail trader is the last seller in the chain and sells in small quantities to the people who use the goods.

markets-around-us.text: Why might some customers prefer to shop in a mall?
options: Goods there can be bought at the lowest prices through bargaining
Malls open for only one day, so the goods are fresh
Malls sell goods only to wholesalers
Many shops and brands are under one roof, in a comfortable air-conditioned place
markets-around-us.explanation: A mall offers many shops, brands and comfort in one building, even though its prices are usually higher.

markets-around-us.text: Assertion (A): An aware consumer checks the expiry date of packed food. Reason (R): Food that has passed its expiry date may not be safe to eat.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
markets-around-us.explanation: Checking the date protects health, since food past its expiry date may be unsafe.

markets-around-us.text: Pooja pays Rs 50 for tomatoes to shopkeeper Geeta, who bought them from a trader, who bought them from a farmer. How does Pooja's money reach the farmer?
options: Each person pays the one before him in the chain and keeps something for his own work, so the farmer gets only a part of Rs 50
Pooja's Rs 50 goes straight to the farmer
The farmer gets more than Rs 50 because of the chain
The money never reaches anyone except the shopkeeper
markets-around-us.explanation: Money passes back along the chain, with each trader keeping a share, so the farmer receives only a part.

markets-around-us.text: Meena's mother buys vegetables and cheap utensils every Saturday from a market that comes up near their town. The traders there go to other places on other days. What kind of market is this?
markets-around-us.explanation: A market held on one fixed day of the week, with traders moving on afterwards, is a weekly market.

markets-around-us.text: At the Tuesday market, Anita asks the seller for Rs 200 for a bag. She offers Rs 150, and they settle at Rs 170. What did she do, and where is it most common?
options: She bargained, which is common in malls with fixed price tags
She took credit, which is common in wholesale markets
She bargained, which is common in weekly markets and with hawkers
She hawked goods, which is common in malls
markets-around-us.explanation: Bargaining is common in weekly markets and with hawkers, while malls usually sell at fixed prices.

markets-around-us.text: Why do many people like going to a weekly market?
options: Every item there carries a fixed price tag, so no thinking is needed
It is open on every day of the year
Only branded goods are sold there
They can find a wide variety of goods at low prices in one place
markets-around-us.explanation: Weekly markets sell many kinds of things, from vegetables to utensils, at low prices and with bargaining.

markets-around-us.text: Assertion (A): Prices in a weekly market are usually lower than in a shop in a mall. Reason (R): Weekly market traders do not have to spend on rent and other costs of a permanent shop.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
markets-around-us.explanation: Traders without a permanent shop have fewer expenses, and that is why they can charge less.

markets-around-us.text: Why do many small cotton farmers sell their crop to a trader at the price the trader offers?
options: They often depend on the trader for loans and need money quickly, so they cannot bargain much
The law says farmers must sell only to traders
Cotton can be sold only on weekly market days
Traders always offer the highest price in the country
markets-around-us.explanation: Small farmers often owe money to the trader and need cash fast, which leaves them with little power to bargain.

markets-around-us.text: Why is it sensible to compare prices at two or three shops before buying an expensive item?
options: All shops must charge the same price, so comparing is only for fun
Prices of the same item can differ from shop to shop, and comparing helps us get a fair price
The item gets cheaper each time we visit a new shop
The cheapest item is always the best in quality
markets-around-us.explanation: Shops may charge different prices for the same item, so comparing helps a consumer pay a fair price.

markets-around-us.text: Why are hawkers useful to people who live in a colony far from the market?
options: They sell goods at prices fixed by the government
They sell only branded goods in air-conditioned stores
They bring goods to people's doorstep
They open a permanent shop in every street
markets-around-us.explanation: Hawkers carry goods to where people live, so buyers do not have to travel to a market.

markets-around-us.text: A wholesale trader is a person who
options: sells goods one by one to consumers
moves from street to street selling goods
grows crops and sells them in the market
buys goods in large quantities and sells them to retail traders
