markets-around-us.explanation: Wholesale traders deal in large lots and supply the retail traders, who then sell to consumers.

markets-around-us.text: Rohan has a toothache and goes to Dr Sharma, who treats him. What is Dr Sharma providing?
markets-around-us.explanation: Treating a patient is work done for someone, so it is a service.

markets-around-us.text: Assertion (A): In a market chain, the price of a product usually rises as it passes from the farmer to the consumer. Reason (R): Each trader in the chain meets his own expenses and earns something for his work.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
markets-around-us.explanation: Each trader adds his costs and earnings, so the price keeps rising along the chain.

markets-around-us.text: Neha sees a shirt at Rs 1200 with a fixed price tag in a mall. At the weekly market, a similar shirt costs Rs 400 and she bargains it down to Rs 350. Which statement best explains the difference?
options: The mall is not allowed to charge less
The mall shop has costs such as rent, air-conditioning and staff that a weekly market stall does not have
Weekly market traders buy their goods at no cost
Shirts are made only for malls
markets-around-us.explanation: A mall shop carries heavy expenses, so it charges more than a stall that has no permanent shop to pay for.

markets-around-us.text: Assertion (A): Only a shopping mall can be called a market. Reason (R): A market is any place where buyers and sellers meet to exchange goods and services.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
markets-around-us.explanation: A is false because weekly markets and neighbourhood shops are markets too, while R is a correct description of a market.

markets-around-us.text: Which order shows a market chain for vegetables grown by a farmer?
markets-around-us.explanation: The vegetables travel from the farmer to a trader, then to a shopkeeper, and finally to the consumer.

markets-around-us.text: Why should you ask for a bill when you buy an item from a shop?
options: The shopkeeper must then give the next item free
It is needed only when you bargain
It is proof of purchase and helps if you want to complain or return the item
markets-around-us.explanation: A bill proves that you bought the item, which helps when there is a problem with it.

markets-around-us.text: Which of these is NOT a feature of a weekly market?
options: Shops are on different floors of an air-conditioned building
It is held on a particular day of the week
Traders do not have a permanent shop
markets-around-us.explanation: Shops on many floors of an air-conditioned building describe a mall, not a weekly market.

markets-around-us.text: Which of these is NOT a retail trader?
options: A trader who sells sacks of wheat only to shopkeepers
A vegetable seller in a weekly market
markets-around-us.explanation: Selling large lots only to shopkeepers is wholesale trading; the others sell to consumers.

markets-around-us.text: A person who buys goods or services for his or her own use is called a
markets-around-us.explanation: A consumer is the person who finally uses the goods or services that are bought.

markets-around-us.text: Assertion (A): Neighbourhood shops are convenient for daily needs. Reason (R): Weekly markets often have lower prices than neighbourhood shops.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
markets-around-us.explanation: Both are true, but lower weekly market prices do not explain why neighbourhood shops are convenient.

markets-around-us.text: Every morning Mrs Joseph, who runs a grocery shop, buys sacks of rice and dal from a trader who sells only to shopkeepers and never to families. What kind of trader is this?
markets-around-us.explanation: A trader who sells large lots to shopkeepers is a wholesale trader.

markets-around-us.text: Which of these is NOT true of shops in a shopping complex?
options: The traders have to move to a new place every day
Many shops are found together in one place
Buyers can find different kinds of goods in the same place
markets-around-us.explanation: Traders in a shopping complex stay in their permanent shops; moving daily is a feature of weekly markets and hawkers.

markets-around-us.text: Assertion (A): A wholesale trader sells goods directly to consumers in small quantities. Reason (R): A wholesale trader buys goods in large quantities.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
markets-around-us.explanation: A is false because wholesalers sell large lots to retailers, but R is true.

markets-around-us.text: Who is a middleman in a market chain?
options: The consumer who buys the final product
A trader who buys goods from producers and sells them on to others
The farmer who grows the crop
The officer who checks weights in the market
markets-around-us.explanation: A middleman stands between the producer and the final buyer, buying and then selling again.

markets-around-us.text: Suresh bought a packet of juice and later saw that its expiry date was last month. Which habit of an aware consumer did he miss?
options: Checking the expiry date before buying
Comparing the colour of the packet
markets-around-us.explanation: An aware consumer reads the label and expiry date before buying packed food.

markets-around-us.text: Lakshmi's neighbours can walk into her small shop at any hour to buy one egg or a small packet of salt. Which feature of neighbourhood shops does this show?
options: They sell only in bulk to other shopkeepers
They move from lane to lane
They open only on one fixed day
They are nearby and sell goods in small quantities as needed
markets-around-us.explanation: Neighbourhood shops are close to home and let people buy just what they need.

markets-around-us.text: Which of these is NOT a good habit of an aware consumer?
options: Buying a packed item without looking at its label or expiry date
Checking the MRP on the packet
Comparing prices before buying a costly item
markets-around-us.explanation: An aware consumer reads labels and expiry dates, so buying without looking is a poor habit.

markets-around-us.text: Raju has two acres of vegetables and sells them to a trader at a low price because he needs money soon. Mr Singh, a large trader, buys from many farmers, stores the goods and sells in the city. Why is Mr Singh likely to earn more than Raju?
options: He works harder than Raju in the field
He has more money and storage, can buy in large amounts and can wait for better prices
The law gives large traders higher prices
markets-around-us.explanation: A large trader with money and storage has more power in the market, while a small farmer in need of cash has little.

markets-around-us.text: Why does a small retail shopkeeper usually buy goods from a wholesale trader instead of going to many farmers and factories?
options: Wholesale traders give goods to shopkeepers for free
The law does not allow shopkeepers to meet producers
The wholesale trader collects many goods in large lots, which saves the shopkeeper time and effort
Wholesale traders sell only to consumers
markets-around-us.explanation: The wholesaler brings together goods from many producers, so the retailer can buy a variety in one place.

markets-around-us.text: Mr Das earns a small daily wage. He wants to buy vegetables and a school bag for his daughter at the lowest price. Which market is the best choice, and why?
options: A mall, because prices there can be bargained
A wholesale trader, because he sells single items
Only a hawker, because hawkers have government fixed rates
The weekly market, because prices are low and bargaining is possible
markets-around-us.explanation: Weekly markets offer low prices and room to bargain, which suits families with small incomes.
